title: Simplified Fe Quantification Assay
author: Opentrons
materials: Pause so user can cover the digestion plate.

steps.title: Set assay mode
steps.instruction: Select Simplified Fe Quantification Assay mode; if Test Mode, skip all incubations and temperature changes.

steps.title: Calibrate deck positions
steps.instruction: User calibrates the protocol on the deck.

steps.title: Verify deck layout
steps.instruction: Confirm samples are in the sample block, an empty digestion plate is in the heating module, and the reagent block contains only water in well A1.

steps.title: Add water to digestion plate
steps.instruction: Pipette a user‑selected volume of 5–20 µL water (same for all samples) in triplicate from the reagent block into each well of the digestion plate using a single 30 µL tip.

steps.title: Add sample aliquots to digestion plate
steps.instruction: Pipette the same 5–20 µL volume (as in the previous step) of each sample in triplicate from the sample block into the digestion plate using 1–24 disposable 30 µL tips.

steps.title: Add nitric acid and mix
steps.instruction: Add 1200 µL of nitric acid from the acid block to each well of the digestion plate, then mix the solution 15 times with a multi‑channel pipette using 200 µL aspirate/dispense volume.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 1200 µL nitric acid into each well.
Mix 15 cycles at 200 µL with multi‑channel pipette.

steps.title: Cover digestion plate
steps.instruction: Pause the protocol and allow the user to cover the digestion plate.

steps.title: Digest at 95 °C
steps.instruction: Raise the heating block to 95 °C (variable per email 12/15/22) and maintain this temperature for 12 h (variable per email 12/15/22).

steps.title: Cool digestion plate
steps.instruction: Cool the heating block to room temperature and wait 1 h to ensure all samples reach ambient temperature.

steps.title: Remove cover and load plates
steps.instruction: Pause for the user to remove the cover from the digestion plate and to place the reagent block and the Quartz analysis plate on the deck.

steps.title: Transfer calibration standards
steps.instruction: Transfer triplicate 10 µL aliquots from the seven Fe calibration standards in the sample block to the Quartz analysis plate in slot 2 (21 wells total) using seven 30 µL tips.

substeps.instruction: Pick up 10 µL from each of the 7 standards (triplicate).
Dispense into designated wells of the Quartz plate.

steps.title: Mix digestion plate columns
steps.instruction: Mix all columns of the digestion plate with a multi‑channel pipette.

steps.title: Transfer sample aliquots to analysis plate
steps.instruction: Transfer 5–20 µL aliquots from each well of the digestion plate to the Quartz analysis plate in slot 2 (6–75 wells, using 6–75 disposable 30 µL tips).

substeps.instruction: Aspirate 5–20 µL from each digestion well.
Dispense into the corresponding well of the Quartz plate.

steps.title: Heat analysis plate to 95 °C
steps.instruction: Raise the heating block to 95 °C and maintain for 1 h.

steps.title: Cool analysis plate
steps.instruction: Cool the heating block to room temperature and wait 1 h to ensure all samples reach ambient temperature.

steps.title: Position plates for detection
steps.instruction: Pause for the user to place the Quartz analysis plate in slot 2 and return the digestion plate to the heating module.

steps.title: Add water to analysis wells
steps.instruction: Add 46 µL of water from the reagent block to each well of the Quartz analysis plate (27–96 wells) using a single 300 µL tip.

steps.title: Add reagent A and mix
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL of reagent A from the reagent block to each well of the Quartz analysis plate (27–96 wells) and mix.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 30 µL reagent A into each well.

steps.title: Incubate reagent A reaction
steps.instruction: Wait 1 h for reagent A to react with Fe in each well.

steps.title: Add reagent B
steps.instruction: Add 49 µL of reagent B from the reagent block to each well of the Quartz analysis plate (27–96 wells) using a single 300 µL tip.

steps.title: Add reagent C and mix
steps.instruction: Add 75 µL of reagent C from the reagent block to each well of the Quartz analysis plate (27–96 wells) and mix.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 75 µL reagent C into each well.
